header.property: properties/123456789 (web stream www.example.com; the app sends to the same property)
header.behaviour_label: graded: 9,450 pricing views, above the 100-view floor

executive_summary.biggest_strength: A clear three-plan ladder: Growth is badged, each step up costs less per staff calendar, and Growth is the plan most customers pay for (47%, from your plan mix).
executive_summary.biggest_blocker: The page never says what taking payments or text reminders costs beyond the plan price: 42.0% of next-page views go to the payments page, and 192 visitors followed the footnote link to the payment partner's site.
executive_summary.quick_win: Add a fees line under the cards and one FAQ answer on card fees and SMS credits.
executive_summary.at_stake: 6,800 visitors read pricing in 30 days and 1,940 clicked a plan; 2,300 next-page views went to the payments page instead of signup (1,650).

scorecard.key_number: 3 key events defined, all 3 fired; no low days (every day above 20% of the best 7-day average of 1,691)
scorecard.why: Conversions are recorded and tracking ran the whole window.

scorecard.key_number: 15.2% of sessions include a pricing view (7,900 of 52,100)
scorecard.why: Pricing is easy to find; the home page is the main way in.

scorecard.key_number: 62s engagement per view vs 48s site; read-to-bottom 40.0% vs 37.0% site
scorecard.why: Visitors read pricing longer than an average page and reach the bottom a little more often.

scorecard.key_number: 42.0% of next-page views go to one information page, the payments feature page
scorecard.why: Visitors leave pricing to answer 'what does taking payments cost?', which the page doesn't.

scorecard.key_number: select_plan fired 2,460 times for 1,940 users (28.5% of pricing users); sign_up fires after it on the app
scorecard.why: Plan choices are measured with a custom event, and a key event follows, so page tests can be read.

scorecard.key_number: mobile 48s per view vs desktop 74s (65%); read-to-bottom 25.1% vs 52.0% (48%)
scorecard.why: Mobile brings 45.5% of pricing views and reads far less of the page.

scorecard.key_number: 3 plans named by stage; price steps 2.6x and 2.0x; cost per staff calendar $19.00, $9.80, $4.95; spread top ÷ entry 5.2x
scorecard.why: A clean good-better-best ladder: each plan says who it is for and costs less per staff calendar than the one below.

scorecard.key_number: Business shown beside the others; yearly saving labelled '2 months free' (16.7% off); monthly selected by default; no crossed-out price, no value figure (noted, not graded)
scorecard.why: A visible top plan and a saving in the usual 15 to 20% band.

scorecard.key_number: each card opens with what it adds over the plan below ('Everything in Starter, plus 5 staff calendars, SMS reminders and deposits'); 7 bullets at most
scorecard.why: The reason to move up is on the card, not only in the table.

scorecard.key_number: Growth carries 'Most popular' and is the plan you want sold; comparison table of 18 rows; mobile capture: Starter fills the first screen and the table scrolls sideways
scorecard.why: Right on desktop, but on a phone the badged plan sits below the first screen and the table loses its plan names.

scorecard.key_number: '4.8/5 from salon and studio owners' and three customer logos under the plan cards; 'Cancel any time' and 'No setup fees' by the buttons
scorecard.why: Proof and risk reducers both sit next to the plans.
Nothing manufactured, which suits a monthly self-serve product.

scorecard.key_number: FAQ with 6 questions; missing: extra costs beyond the plan price (card processing fees, SMS reminder credits)
scorecard.why: The one question sales hears most has no answer on the page.

scorecard.key_number: all 3 plan buttons say 'Start free' and go to app.example.com/signup with the plan in the link; button contrast passes on the capture
scorecard.why: The same label on every card doesn't say which plan the click starts.

behaviour_report.channel_reading: Email sessions engage most (85.3%) and Organic Social least (56.2%); every channel has 10 or more sessions.

engagement.note: Scroll fires once at 90% depth, so read-to-bottom means reached the bottom, not a depth curve.

landing_on_pricing.note: above 1.5 pages per session: people who land on pricing go on to other pages

new_vs_returning.note: returning visitors spend about 1.9x longer per view: they come back to compare before buying (reported, not graded)

improvements.issue: Visitors leave to find out what payments cost
improvements.evidence: 2,300 of 5,480 next-page views (42.0%) go to the payments feature page, and 210 outbound clicks from pricing follow the footnote link to the payment partner's site.
improvements.why_it_costs: Each visitor who leaves to check fees is one more step away from a plan, and some never come back.
improvements.fix: Add one line under the cards: what card payments cost per transaction and how SMS reminders are counted on each plan.

improvements.evidence: The FAQ has 6 questions: billing, plan changes, what counts as a staff member, plan fit, contracts and support. Nothing on card fees or SMS credits, the two questions sales hears most.
improvements.why_it_costs: Buyers who suspect hidden costs pick the cheapest plan or wait.
improvements.fix: Add the two questions listed under rewrites, near the top of the FAQ.

improvements.issue: Mobile visitors read much less of the page
improvements.evidence: Mobile: 48s per view and 25.1% read-to-bottom, against 74s and 52.0% on desktop. Mobile is 45.5% of pricing views.
improvements.why_it_costs: Most of the comparison, the proof and the FAQ sit where mobile visitors don't reach.
improvements.fix: See B4: put Growth first on mobile and replace the sideways table with one list per plan.

improvements.issue: On a phone the badged plan is below the first screen
improvements.evidence: Cards stack in plan order, so Starter fills the first screen and Growth's badge shows only after one scroll. The 18-row comparison table scrolls sideways; the plan names leave the screen as it scrolls.
improvements.why_it_costs: Center stage only works when the middle plan is seen first.
improvements.fix: On mobile, show Growth first (or open the page on it), and turn the table into a 'compare plans' list per plan.

improvements.issue: One generic button label on every plan
improvements.why_it_costs: The label doesn't confirm which plan the click starts.
improvements.fix: Name the plan on each button (rewrites below).

tier_by_tier.recommendation: Say who outgrows it: a second staff member or SMS reminders means Growth.

tier_by_tier.adds_over_plan_below: 5 staff calendars, SMS reminders and deposits
tier_by_tier.recommendation: Keep the badge; show '$9.80 per staff calendar' on the card.

tier_by_tier.adds_over_plan_below: 20 staff calendars, several locations and priority support
tier_by_tier.recommendation: Name the multi-location use on the card, and move the 'Talk to us' link for 20+ staff onto it.

pricing_psychology.note: Business sits beside the others at 5.2x the Starter price.
Growth is badged and in the middle; on mobile it falls below Starter (B4).
Three plans with a clear middle already steer buyers.
Business, for busy locations, makes Growth read as the solid choice for a small team.
Cost per staff calendar falls 48% from Starter to Growth and 49% from Growth to Business, but the cards never say so.
Prices are shown per month, which feels smaller than a yearly total.
'2 months free' is clear; test adding the yearly amount saved per plan ($38, $98, $198).
$19, $49 and $99 end just below round numbers, which suits small business buyers.
Right unless a real past price exists. Never show an invented one.
No figure on what a missed appointment costs. Test one line on Growth (for example, what SMS reminders save in no-shows) using only numbers the business can back.

rewrites.tier_names: Keep. Starter, Growth and Business say which step each plan is.

taglines.tagline: For one pro taking their own bookings.
For a small team that wants fewer no-shows.
For busy locations with a front desk.

faq_to_add: What does it cost to take card payments and deposits?
Do SMS reminders cost extra, and how many are included?
rewrites.fees_line: Under the cards: 'Card payments: [the processor's rate] per transaction. SMS reminders: [what each plan includes].' Fill in the real figures.

ab_tests.hypothesis: If the page states card fees and SMS costs, then select_plan per pricing user rises from 28.5%, because 42.0% of next-page views leave to find that out.
ab_tests.metric: select_plan users ÷ pricing users; share of next-page views to the payments page

ab_tests.hypothesis: If mobile opens on Growth, then mobile select_plan for Growth rises, because the badge sits below the first screen today and mobile reads to the bottom at 25.1%.

ab_tests.test: Cost per staff calendar on the cards
ab_tests.hypothesis: If Growth and Business show their cost per staff calendar, then more buyers choose them, because the per-unit price falls 48% and 49% and the page never says so.
If each button names its plan, then select_plan per pricing user rises, because the next step is clearer.
